Order:

The present criminal petition, under Section 482 Cr.P.C., is filed by the petitioner-accused No. 2 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No. 212 of 2016 on the file of the Court of learned Additional Judicial I Class Magistrate, Addanki (for short, 'the trial Court'), registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 193, 342, 420, 421, 427, 449 and 464 read with Section 34 IPC.

entities.text: Additional Judicial I Class Magistrate, Addanki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri B.S.Shivaji, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner-accused No. 2, Sri M.S.N.Prasad, learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 1-complainant, and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No. 2-State.
3.

Respondent No. 1 filed a private complaint against accused Nos. 1 to 5 alleging that he is the owner of house property situated in R.S.No. 244/2B of Muppavaram Village, J.Pangulur Mandal,
Prakasam District, adjacent to NH-5.

In the year 2001, National Highways Authority of India (for short, 'NHAI'), for the purpose of widening of road into four lanes, acquired the land of respondent No. 1 which is in an extent of Ac. 0.00  cent along with house portion and consequently,
respondent No. 1 adjusted his portion towards east by leaving the acquired portion.

Further, in the year 2011, NHAI once again proposed to widen the very same road from four lanes to six lanes and as part of widening process, NHAI acquired an extent of 20.24 square meters of land belonging to respondent No. 1.
Compensation was awarded only with regard to the land but no compensation was awarded towards house property.

It is further alleged that on 07-01-2014, accused Nos. 1 to 3 along with accused No. 4 came to the house of respondent No. 1 and told that they proposed to demolish his house portion but the accused did not choose to provide time required by him to vacate the house.
They forcibly demolished the house of respondent No. 1 causing loss to household articles worth about Rs.25,000/-.

It is also alleged that the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition,
NH-5, Ongole, Prakasam District, passed an award only for the site without granting compensation towards structures on the site.

It is stated that NHAI issued notice of award under Section 3 H (2) of the National Highways Laws (Amendment) Act, 1997 (for short, 'the Act'), to respondent No. 1 by informing that the latter was awarded an amount of Rs.7,000/- towards compensation for acquisition of the land in an extent of 20.24 square meters situated in R.S.No. 244/2B of Muppavaram Village, J.Pangulur Mandal, Prakasam District, but the former did not pay any compensation towards structures.

As such, the grievance of respondent No. 1 is that without A.V.Rao vs Velagapudi Venkata Ramamurthy And ... on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184098456/
1 awarding any compensation, his house property was demolished for the purpose of widening of road into six lanes.
Learned counsel, therefore, prays to allow the criminal petition.

5. On the other hand, Sri M.S.N.Prasad, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.
1-complainant, and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No. 2-State vehemently opposed the criminal petition.
6. This Court has considered the rival submissions put forward by learned counsel on either side.

As seen from the material available on record, NHAI acquired land in an extent of Ac. 0.00  cent along with structures thereon belonging to respondent No. 1 in the year 2002 itself and an award was also passed on 15-07-2022 granting compensation of Rs.87,749/- which was accepted by respondent No. 1.
When once the structures were already acquired and demolished during the first phase of road widening, question of demolishing the same again on 07-01-2014 does not arise.
Respondent No. 1 is not entitled for compensation twice for the very same structures.
7. Further, the petitioner-accused No. 2 is working as Project Director and he is a public servant but no sanction has been obtained before prosecuting him.
In the light of the above facts and circumstances of the case, continuation of proceedings against the petitioner-accused No. 2 is therefore nothing but an abuse of process of law.
8. Accordingly, the proceedings against the petitioner-accused No. 2 in C.C.No. 212 of 2016 on the file of the Court of learned Additional Judicial I Class Magistrate, Addanki, are hereby quashed.
